tasks.short: Classify and register artifacts and supervise inventory

steps.what: Inspect actual artifacts and their available accession evidence to establish identity, distinguishing features and provenance limits.
Capture the actual object description and accession-source references in a draft in the collections-management system {OTHER}.
inputs: Actual observations and evidence from s1

steps.what: Look up current classification terms and comparable collection records in the collections-management system {OTHER}.
inputs: Existing classification scheme and collection records
outputs: Relevant authorised terms and comparison records

steps.what: Classify artifacts from the actual object and evidence, selecting the appropriate authorised terms and recording uncertainty in the collection draft {OTHER}.
outputs: Actual classification decision in the object draft

steps.what: Assign a proposed registration number to the artifact draft from the existing numbering sequence and uniqueness rules in the collections-management system {OTHER}.
inputs: Existing numbering sequence and registered identifiers
outputs: Completed registration draft with unique proposed number

steps.what: Check the completed registration draft against actual object identity, classification evidence, accession source and numbering rules.
Commit the exact checked artifact registration and assigned number in the collections-management system {OTHER}.
Read actual inventory movements, count results and unresolved discrepancies in the collections-management system {OTHER} before directing inventory work.
inputs: Existing actual inventory records and count results

steps.what: Supervise inventory control through actual staff discussion, spot checks and direction on unresolved artifact location or identity discrepancies.
inputs: Actual staff work and collection conditions
outputs: Actual supervision and decisions on follow-up

tasks.design: Configure native classification views, numbering rules and inventory exception views in the collections-management system {OTHER}. Object examination, actual description, classification and inventory supervision remain human; a proposed number is checked before its separate commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Authorised terms, registration sequences and inventory exceptions are manually found and cross-checked.
tasks.enabler_now: Native controlled terms, numbering and filtered inventory views.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain provenance, ambiguous objects and real inventory discrepancies.
tasks.human_edge: Examining the object and directing responsible inventory work.

ambition.what: No automated provenance or authenticity judgment is assumed.

tasks.altitude: Less mechanical lookup and numbering, with collection authority unchanged.

evidence.claim: Collection-system configuration can support controlled-term lookup, unique numbering and inventory exception views while object judgment remains human.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual object work, registration and the focal worker's inventory supervision. Shares are conditional E1 estimates, not measured museum baselines.

Worker produces actual observations in s1 and description in s2. Existing collection governance supplies term ids, numbering sequence and uniqueness rules. Existing inventory processes supply actual object id, movement, location, count and discrepancy records; their capture and staff labour are unchanged outside the claimed saving. Missing records require manual verification, not inferred presence.

Test native configuration first. s5 only replaces actual manual number selection where that burden exists; already automatic numbering earns no saving. Lookup and inventory views reduce retrieval only, not classification, physical labelling, stock counting or supervision. No new formal supervision report is assumed.
The ordinary final registration check supplies the requested exact-version gate without extra self-approval labour; edits void it. Commit time is short and fully retained.
research_questions: Do native views and sequence rules remove actual clerical work while exposing unresolved object and inventory uncertainty?

already_counted.description: Actual examination, description, residual lookup, classification, final check, commit and supervision remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain term, sequence and inventory-view mappings.

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed object registration checked in s6

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 10 x 40% term retrieval + 10 actual numbering + 8 x 50% inventory retrieval = 18 gross less 1.5 upkeep. Already configured systems yield no benefit; object judgment and supervision retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Construct mounts, replicas or duplicate specimens

steps.what: Read the actual object history and relevant construction or conservation references in {DOCS} for the proposed skeletal mount, replica or duplicate specimen.
Examine actual fossils, archaeological artifacts or specimens and the available materials, establishing physical constraints for the proposed construction.
outputs: Actual measurements, observations and construction constraints

steps.what: Draw and check the actual object-specific construction plan and material choices against observed constraints before working with the object.
inputs: Actual measurements and constraints from s2

steps.what: Construct skeletal mounts of fossils, replicas of archaeological artifacts, or duplicate specimens, using a variety of materials and hand tools within the checked plan.
outputs: Actual constructed mount, replica or duplicate specimen

steps.what: Inspect the actual completed construction for fit, condition and fidelity, correcting the physical work where needed.
Write and check the actual construction materials, method and observed result in the existing collection-work record {OTHER}.
inputs: Actual construction and inspected result from s4-s5

steps.what: Save the exact checked construction record in the collections-management system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Retain the actual examination, object-specific planning and hand-tool construction. Check native reference views in {DOCS} and collection-work fields in {OTHER}; this bespoke project still needs source appraisal and a new factual record, so no labour reduction is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on actual object condition and physical craftsmanship.
tasks.enabler_now: No software change is justified by this construction workflow alone.
tasks.still_hard: Fit, conservation constraints and fidelity to the actual specimen.

ambition.what: No digital fabrication or new service is assumed.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in construction work or authority.

evidence.claim: Bespoke mounts and replicas require actual object examination and hand-tool work; generic document software does not perform that work.

assumptions: Boundary covers an actual bespoke construction and its existing brief collection-work record. Shares are E1 workflow estimates. No extra report, approval board or digital-fabrication baseline is invented.

Worker produces actual measurements and constraints in s2, a real plan in s3, finished physical work in s4-s5 and factual method/result text in s6. Existing references supply source identity and history; missing details require manual examination or source reading, fully counted.

Native source views and record fields are checked before declaring zero. The short source step is substantive project-specific reading; the short record is new construction evidence rather than repeated metadata. No repeated transfer, generic drafting or digital production step is established here.

Existing plan checking supplies the construction boundary gate, and ordinary completed-record checking supplies the requested save gate; no added self-approval labour. Changes void those gates. No new system means zero incremental upkeep; existing runtime and saves earn no saving.
unknowns: Whether a different project has real repeated digital drafting
research_questions: Does observation reveal a genuine repeated drawing or record-transfer step beyond the bespoke physical work?

already_counted.description: All actual source, examination, drawing, construction, physical inspection and separate record work remains counted.

incremental.description: No new workflow or tool to maintain.

approvals.approved_version: Exact object-specific construction plan checked in s3
Exact actual construction record checked in s6

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero after separately checking source lookup, actual drawing, physical construction and factual record writing against native options. No established repeated digital labour is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead tours and teach public courses

steps.what: Find and read current approved object histories and educational source material in {DOCS} for the actual tour or course audience.
inputs: Existing approved object histories and teaching material

steps.what: Adapt the actual route, explanation and educational activities to the students or public audience and current collection access.
Lead tours and teach educational courses to students and the general public, responding to actual questions and understanding.
Write and check the actual completed session's brief existing delivery entry in the museum programme record {OTHER}.
Save the exact checked actual session entry in the museum programme record {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure native topic, object and audience views in {DOCS} for approved educational sources. The worker adapts and delivers the actual session, then writes its brief existing delivery record in {OTHER}; no automated narration or attendance inference is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approved object information is found across separate teaching folders.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting explanations to visitors and responding to unexpected questions.
tasks.human_edge: Presence, storytelling and observing actual understanding.

ambition.what: No larger teaching programme is assumed.

tasks.altitude: Slightly less source finding; teaching authority and delivery remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native document tags can support approved teaching-source retrieval while live tours remain human.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual preparation, tour/course delivery and a brief existing programme entry. Shares are E1 estimates; no newly invented attendance report or per-visitor administrative baseline.

Existing source owners supply object id, topic, audience and approved source version. Worker selects actual context in s1-s2 and produces actual completed delivery in s3. Missing tags require manual source reading; a calendar end never proves completion.

Test native views first. Saving applies only to actual source retrieval, not live teaching, adaptation, record writing or short save. The ordinary completed-entry check supplies the requested save gate without extra self-approval time; edits void it.
research_questions: Does native object and audience filtering reduce actual lookup without flattening historical uncertainty?

already_counted.description: Residual lookup, actual adaptation, live teaching and separate record work remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain approved-source topic and audience tags.

approvals.approved_version: Exact actual delivery entry checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 10 x 30% source retrieval reduction = 3 gross less 0.5 upkeep. Already organised material yields zero; live teaching and record tails retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Physical collection work, object classification and public teaching remain human.
role.ambitious_version: A collection worker who reduces mechanical numbering and lookup while preserving object knowledge, craftsmanship and live teaching.
